source_links.title: SPRING trial
SPRING study protocol
SPRING secondary microbiome analysis and funding
SPRING ketone secondary analysis and product donation

locator: primary abstract; protocol intervention/secondary outcomes; secondary analysis funding/COI
finding: SPRING randomized overweight or obese pregnant participants in Brisbane. GG plus BB-12 strains; preeclampsia secondary outcome, 9.2% vs 4.9%, p=.09. NHMRC and hospital foundation support reported; Chr Hansen supplied active/placebo products in same-cohort report.
limitation: Primary abstract supports percentages, not complete PE adjudication or funding extraction; do not count secondary reports as new trials.

source_links.title: Lindsay probiotic trial
Lindsay 2014 conference report

locator: primary abstract and conference report methods/funding
finding: Dublin trial recruited 175 participants with BMI 30–39.9; 138 completed (63 vs75); L. salivarius UCC118 from weeks 24–28. National Maternity Hospital Medical Fund and Ivo Drury Award in conference disclosure.
limitation: Prior Cochrane PE denominators 62/74 differ from completer totals. Do not replace them or transfer funding from Lindsay 2015 GDM treatment trial.
content_implication: retain research-draft status

source_links.title: HUMBA trial
HUMBA publisher report
HUMBA study protocol

locator: primary abstract; publisher funding; protocol acknowledgments
finding: HUMBA factorial diet/probiotic trial in New Zealand, BMI ≥30, weeks 12–17+6 at randomization; GG and BB12, minimum 6.5 billion CFU in report. Multiple public/charitable/institutional funding sources; Chr Hansen supplied capsules; Roche supplied testing support in protocol.
limitation: Protocol dose differs slightly from report; preeclampsia endpoint omission in broader review unresolved. In-kind support is not proof of biased result.
content_implication: retain research-draft status

source_links.title: Pellonperä fish oil/probiotic trial
Pellonperä cohort 24-month follow-up

locator: primary abstract; same-cohort follow-up methods and funding
finding: Finnish factorial trial randomized 439, mean gestation 13.9 weeks. HN001 and B. lactis 420 strains; follow-up reports 10^10 CFU each, DuPont identified as product source, academy/hospital/foundation grants.
limitation: Funding from follow-up may not capture all primary disclosures; do not infer donation or sponsor role without direct statement.
content_implication: retain research-draft status

source_links.title: Probiotics to prevent gestational diabetes mellitus | Cochrane
The effects of probiotics administration during pregnancy on preeclampsia and associated maternal, fetal, and newborn outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
Probiotics in overweight or obese pregnant women systematic review
2022 probiotic GDM prevention systematic review
New Zealand Medsafe MARC March 2023 remarks

locator: review abstracts, review funding and committee remarks
finding: 2021 Cochrane narrow review shows PE RR 1.85 (1.04–3.29); 2024 broader review RR 1.14 (.84–1.53), 11 trials 2401. 2022 overweight/obesity review RR 1.91 (1.03–3.55) for PE including superimposed; 2022 broader GDM-prevention review did not identify significant PE effect. New Zealand MARC March 2023 judged causal link not established. McDougall review funded by Gates Foundation and Harry Secomb Foundation.
limitation: Overlapping studies, different inclusion/outcome definitions and certainty; committee assessment predates broader 2024 review. Neither null-significance nor regulatory judgment establishes harmlessness.
content_implication: Do not present independent votes or universal harm/safety; no routine supplement recommendation for GDM prevention.

source_links.title: Is taking calcium supplements during pregnancy an effective way to prevent blood pressure disorders and related problems? | Cochrane
Trial trustworthiness assessment: commentary on the Cochrane 2025 systematic review on calcium supplementation during pregnancy
WHO guideline development group: calcium supplementation for prevention of pre-eclampsia
Calcium supplementation and risk of preeclampsia in Ecuadorian pregnant teenagers
Calcium supplementation and prevention of pregnancy induced hypertension

locator: 2025 DOI-version abstract; critique Figure 1 text; original abstracts; WHO notice
finding: 2025 review RR .83 (.67–1.04), 6 RCTs 15364; critique adds disputed studies, not independent synthesis. Lopez-Jaramillo trial enrolled pregnant teenagers in Ecuador and tested 2 g/day. Purwar abstract reports PE RR .13 (.01–.64), whereas critique secondary extraction .17 (.04–.77); keep both provenance labels and do not silently substitute. WHO convened guideline development meeting Aug 11–12 2026.
limitation: Publisher summary page also exposes obsolete older results; use version-specific DOI. Primary full reports, ethics and denominator reconciliation still outstanding. Meeting announcement is not new final guidance.
content_implication: Use DOI version and flag conflicting Purwar estimate; do not turn WHO process into new dosing guidance.

source_links.title: [Table, WHO recommendation: calcium supplementation during pregnancy for prevention of pre-eclampsia and its complications []].
WHO guideline development group: calcium supplementation for prevention of pre-eclampsia
Preconception calcium review

locator: WHO 2018 recommendation table; 2026 notice; 2025 review abstract
finding: Existing WHO low-intake population recommendation and new review process must be distinguished; before-pregnancy calcium review has one trial, composite PE or pregnancy loss RR .85 (.67–1.07).
limitation: No three-year prophylactic indication; updated recommendation not confirmed.
content_implication: Show jurisdiction/date and intended outcome.

source_links.title: ADORE DHA trial
ADORE randomized controlled trial protocol
ORIP baseline omega-3 analysis
A Randomized Trial of Prenatal n−3 Fatty Acid Supplementation and Preterm Delivery

locator: ADORE abstract funding; protocol; ORIP secondary abstract
finding: ADORE compares 1000 vs 200 mg DHA, not placebo; NICHD funded, DSM supplied all capsules. In high baseline status, early PTB 4/289 vs3/271, posterior probability .57. ORIP baseline subgroup shares primary cohort.
limitation: Dose comparator, baseline status and adaptive design matter; no universal supplement protocol.

source_links.title: Office of Dietary Supplements - Dietary Supplements and Life Stages: Pregnancy
Stephens et al. protein requirements in early and late gestation
USDA evidence review protein requirements, Appendix H table 2

locator: ODS Tables 1–2; primary abstract; USDA table H.2
finding: IAAO protein EAR estimate 1.22 g/kg/d (95% CI .79–1.66) at weeks 11–20 (17 analyzed,35 observations); 1.52 (1.28–1.77) at 31–38 weeks (19 analyzed,43 observations).
limitation: Small metabolic requirement study; not a clinical outcome trial, not a personalized protein prescription or official replacement DRI.

source_links.title: Office of Dietary Supplements - Dietary Supplements and Life Stages: Pregnancy
Association of a vegan diet during pregnancy with maternal and child outcomes
NICHD Understanding Eating Behaviors During Twin Pregnancies
Maternal Diet and Breastfeeding | Breastfeeding special circumstances | CDC

locator: ODS special considerations; vegan review abstract; NICHD summary; CDC maternal diet
finding: Vegetarian/vegan diet requires attention to B12, iron, zinc, iodine, calcium, vitamin D, protein, choline and fatty acids; twin needs differ and evidence for specific targets is limited. CDC lactation iodine 290 mcg and choline 550 mg; additional energy 330–400 kcal/day for well-nourished breastfeeding mothers compared with pre-pregnancy.
limitation: Diet context, age, plurality and feeding pattern matter; no automatic supplement or calorie prescription.
content_implication: Separate pregnancy, lactation and special-population references.

source_links.title: Recommendation: Iron Deficiency and Iron Deficiency Anemia During Pregnancy: Screening and Supplementation | United States Preventive Services Taskforce
WHO antenatal iron supplementation
Daily oral iron supplementation during pregnancy

locator: USPSTF recommendation; WHO antenatal iron guidance
finding: US USPSTF I statement for routine screening and supplementation in asymptomatic pregnancy concerns clinical outcomes; WHO population prevention guidance recommends 30–60 mg elemental iron with 400 mcg folic acid daily. ODS total intake reference is not a supplemental dose.
limitation: Different jurisdiction and clinical question; diagnosed deficiency requires care; do not combine doses or apply a global recommendation automatically.
content_implication: retain research-draft status

source_links.title: Biophysical effects, safety and efficacy of raspberry leaf in pregnancy
Office of Dietary Supplements - Dietary Supplements and Life Stages: Pregnancy

locator: integrative review; ODS botanical section
finding: Raspberry leaf RCT enrolled 192 low-risk nulliparous women, from week 32; no significant difference in labor duration or birth mode in ODS summary.
limitation: Human and animal evidence heterogeneous; no reliable safety or efficacy recommendation.
content_implication: Add optional research-only intervention, no dosing instructions.

source_links.title: Use of a specific anti-stretch mark cream for preventing or reducing the severity of striae gravidarum. Randomized, double-blind, controlled trial
Topical preparations for preventing stretch marks in pregnancy | Cochrane

locator: primary trial abstract and review
finding: Specific cream combines hydroxyprolisilane-C, rosehip oil, Centella triterpenes and vitamin E; overall incidence 37.6% treated vs 33.3% control, nonsignificant.
limitation: Subgroup does not demonstrate isolated vitamin E, Centella or shea efficacy; no isolated trial located in targeted search.
content_implication: Keep individual ingredient entries uncertain.

source_links.title: Effects of Collagen Supplements on Skin Aging: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
Oral Collagen Peptides and Skin Rejuvenation: A Systematic Review and an Updated Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
2026 technical reanalysis of collagen reviews
Oral supplementation of specific collagen peptides has beneficial effects on human skin physiology: a double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
The Oral Intake of Specific Bovine-Derived Bioactive Collagen Peptides Has a Stimulatory Effect on Dermal Matrix Synthesis and Improves Various Clinical Skin Parameters

locator: 2025 review abstract; 2026 review publisher excerpt; Grimes/Mahto abstract and Fig 1; primary trial abstract
finding: 2026 technical reanalysis finds inaccurate primary extraction and incompatible measures; dose meta-regression did not establish benefit. Hydration p=.08, elasticity p=.92; heterogeneity 58.8% and 98.6% respectively. Authors report no COI. Proksch 2014: 69 adult women, 23 each across two dose arms and placebo, 8 weeks.
limitation: Reanalysis challenges two identified reviews, not proof all trials invalid. Shared placebo and outcome/timepoint correlation matter. No pregnancy prevention endpoint; complete arm means/SD still pending.
content_implication: Do not graph funding subgroups as independent estimates or count multiple dose arms as independent controls.

source_links.title: The Oral Intake of Specific Bovine-Derived Bioactive Collagen Peptides Has a Stimulatory Effect on Dermal Matrix Synthesis and Improves Various Clinical Skin Parameters

locator: full article abstract, exclusions, funding, COI
finding: 2025 RCT 66 women aged 35–55, 33 per group; 8 weeks; pregnancy/lactation excluded. Product supplied by GELITA; sponsor role reported limited; author reports supported lectures and patents. No adverse events reported in small adult trial.
limitation: No rare-harm or pregnancy safety inference; product-specific adult findings; complete numerical arm extraction not performed.
content_implication: Display product supply, author interests and pregnancy exclusion together.

source_links.title: Effect of hypopressive and conventional abdominal exercises on postpartum diastasis recti: A randomized controlled trial
Hypopressive exercises for diastasis recti and pelvic floor symptoms in postpartum women: A randomized trial
Diastasis exercise network meta-analysis
Core muscle strength and stability-oriented breathing training in postpartum women
Effect of inspiratory plus expiratory neuromuscular electrical stimulation on postpartum diastasis

locator: primary abstracts and accessible indexed methods
finding: 2024 hypopressive vs conventional RCT no significant group main effect at two measurement sites; within-condition changes differ. 2026 hypopressive trial reports prone bridge between-group difference 34 s (13–55), side tests 12 s (3–21),16 s (7–25), body appreciation 9 (5–13), pelvic complaints −4 (−6 to −2). 2025 breathing and NMES trials identified.
limitation: Separate site, condition and outcome; full samples, timepoints, baseline/harms need extraction. No inference of routine pregnancy NMES safety.
content_implication: Prioritize function rather than gap alone; new trials are distinct only after registry/cross-publication check.

source_links.title: Acupuncture as an adjunct to standard treatment for pelvic girdle pain in pregnant women: randomised double-blinded controlled trial comparing acupuncture with non-penetrating sham acupuncture
Effects of acupuncture and stabilising exercises as adjunct to standard treatment in pregnant women with pelvic girdle pain: randomised single blind controlled trial

locator: primary sham-trial abstract
finding: Sham-controlled trial median pain VAS changed 66 to36 vs69 to41; between-group pain comparison p=.493.
limitation: Both arms improved; active vs sham did not establish specific analgesic advantage. Adjunct standard-care comparator is a different question.
content_implication: Show sham comparison in acupuncture record.

source_links.title: Evaluation of postpartum pelvic floor physical therapy on obstetrical anal sphincter injury
Obstetric anal sphincter injury and female sexual dysfunction
Sexual function at 6 and 12 months after OASI and physical therapy

locator: RCT and systematic review excerpts; observational abstract
finding: OASI rehabilitation is a separate population. Systematic review describes substantial dyspareunia and sexual dysfunction after severe injury; did not establish significant physical-therapy impact on sexual dysfunction. Observational comparison cannot establish causality.
limitation: Bladder/bowel symptoms, quality of life and sexual function are separate endpoints. No universal exercise protocol.
content_implication: Offer assessment and symptom-based care; no deadline for resuming sex.

source_links.title: Double-blind randomized trial of niacinamide 4% vs hydroquinone 4% for melasma
Update on Melasma—Part II: Treatment
Visible light protection and melasma relapse
Evaluation of the effectiveness of a broad-spectrum sunscreen in the prevention of chloasma in pregnant women

locator: split-face trial; review; prior pregnancy cohort
finding: 4% niacinamide vs 4% hydroquinone trial in melasma is not a pregnancy prevention study. Review describes niacinamide as pregnancy/lactation compatible but direct pregnancy clinical outcome evidence remains limited.

source_links.title: Cosmetic Dermatology in Pregnancy and Lactation: A Risk–Benefit Framework for Clinical Practice
A review of the safety of cosmetic procedures during pregnancy and lactation

locator: 2026 review publisher text; earlier review abstract
finding: Newer review distinguishes pregnancy from lactation, describes PRP cosmetic pregnancy evidence as lacking and low-level photobiomodulation as low theoretical exposure with caution.
